facts.content: Patient presents with progressive shortness of breath for approximately two weeks, worse in the last few days, and dyspnea on exertion with minimal activity around the house.
facts.source_text: • CC: Progressive SOB x ~2 wks; worse last few days; DOE with minimal exertion/around house

facts.content: Patient reports a mild dry cough.
Patient reports bilateral ankle swelling for a few days.
Patient denies chest pain, palpitations, and fever.
Patient reports that appetite is okay.
Patient reports frequent urination.
Patient has a history of heart failure.
Patient reports a prior small heart attack about five years ago with brief hospitalization.
facts.source_text: prior “small heart attack” ~5 yrs ago (per pt; brief hospitalization)

facts.content: Patient is taking furosemide, dose unknown.
Patient is taking aspirin.
Patient is taking metoprolol.
Patient is taking simvastatin.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father died of a heart attack in his early sixties.

facts.content: Patient's mother is alive and has osteoporosis.
Patient lives alone.
Patient works part-time as a lorry driver on day shifts.

Patient does not drink alcohol.
Patient used to walk to the shops daily but is now limited by shortness of breath.

facts.content: Clinician reports chest examination is normal.
Clinician reports blood pressure is okay.
Clinician reports oxygen saturation is okay.

facts.source_text: 1) HF exacerbation — progressive SOB/DOE, new bilateral ankle edema; mild dry cough; no CP/fever; exam BP/SpO2 OK

facts.content: Clinician notes a history of prior myocardial infarction about five years ago as reported by the patient.

facts.content: Plan is to increase furosemide to one tablet twice daily for several days and monitor symptoms.

facts.content: Plan is to obtain blood tests today including full blood count and renal function (urea and electrolytes).
Plan is to order a transthoracic echocardiogram in one to two weeks.
Safety net advice is to seek care if worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.

facts.content: Patient is to follow up in one week for reassessment.
